response.text: Your goal is to build a Python script that runs once a day, pulls the previous day's orders from your Shopify store through the API, and adds them to a Google Sheet including order number, date, customer email, items, total, and fulfilment status, while skipping duplicate orders and writing an execution log. I will deliver a Python script connecting to the Shopify API, rate limit handling, an execution log, skip duplicate order logic, Google Sheets integration, and daily scheduling. First, I will write the Python script to connect to the Shopify API, fetch the previous day's orders, parse order details, and check against existing Google Sheet records to skip duplicates. Second, I will implement rate limit handling for the Shopify API and add a logging mechanism for script execution verification. Third, I will configure the daily scheduling mechanism for the script and test the end-to-end data pull into Google Sheets. I would schedule it using a standard system scheduler, and I would handle Shopify API rate limits by implementing retry logic with exponential backoff when hitting API throttling thresholds. I did nearly this for a warehouse database: I wrote a Python service that listens to Shopify inventory webhooks, reconciles counts against PostgreSQL on a schedule and logs every change, resulting in stock synced every 15 minutes, with no oversold orders in the first month. Which hosting environment do you prefer for running the daily scheduled Python script?
